jobs.occupation: The Danish School of Education (DPU) at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University, invites applications for a position as an associate professor in educational and developmental psychology, commencing on 1 March 2027.
jobs.description:
Associate Professor in Educational and Developmental Psychology  

This is a full-time position commencing on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The position is based at DPU, at either the Aarhus campus or the Emdrup campus in Copenhagen. The selected applicant will be expected to participate in day-to-day activities at the school, including teaching and supervision. Some travel should be expected between the school’s campuses in Aarhus and Copenhagen. 

The position  

The position involves research and university teaching in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will help further develop the existing research and teaching environment within the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, with a particular focus on developmental psychology in early childhood. 

The position involves teaching at Master’s level and conducting research in the fields of educational and developmental psychology. The selected applicant will become part of a well-established academic environment within the Department 

The selected applicant should be able to document experience conducting empirical research, both independently and in collaboration with others, including studies within childhood developmental psychology, using qualitative, quantitative and/or mixed methods. 

Preference will be given to applicants who can document an interest in one or more of the following research areas: Transitions between institutions and families; family life, children’s psychological, emotional and relational development in and across different settings. 

Preference will be given to applicants able to teach and supervise in psychological and educational assessments and psychometrics. 

Research  

The selected applicant will be expected to: 

• develop new research projects relevant to the field of educational and developmental psychology 
• contribute to collaborative research initiatives at DPU, both nationally and internationally 
• pursue external research funding 
• contribute to theoretical, methodological and empirical developments in the fields of early childhood and/or childhood studies and/or family studies. 
• Applicants must outline their vision and plans for contributing to the suggested research fields. 
Teaching  

The selected applicant will teach and supervise students at all levels across relevant degree programmes at DPU, particularly the Master’s degree programme in educational psychology, including the specialisation in educational psychological counselling (PPR) and related electives, as well as in the field of early childhood. Teaching may also be expected on the professional Master’s degree programme in well-being. 

Talent development  

Associate professors at DPU/AU are expected to continuously develop their competences in supervising students at the Master’s and PhD levels, including the development and teaching of PhD courses focusing on theory, methodology and/or specific methods in collaboration with colleagues. Applicants are invited to describe their experiences of and plans or ideas for talent development. 

Knowledge exchange  

The selected applicant will be expected to engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy of the Faculty of Arts, for instance through collaboration on research with external partners, public dissemination activities, consultancy work or collaboration with relevant stakeholders. Applicants should document any prior experience of knowledge exchange activities and outline their plans for maximising the impact of their research within educational and developmental psychology and its implications for practice. 

Qualifications  

Applicants must hold a PhD degree or equivalent qualifications in a relevant field and be able to document: 

• a research profile within developmental psychology in the fields of daycare/reception class and/or family life, as well as children’s psychological and relational development in early childhood 
• an international publication profile, including experience of participation in international networks 
• experience applying for and obtaining external research funding 
• knowledge of and interest in psychodynamic–relational theories of personality, identity and selfhood from a developmental perspective, whether from a supportive and/or a critical position. 
• experience conducting empirical research, preferably using a range of methodologies relevant to the field of developmental psychology 
• knowledge of psychological tests and assessment tools relevant to early childhood and developmental psychology. 
Further information  
For further information about the position, please contact the head of the Department of Educational Anthropology and Educational Psychology, Charlotte Mathiassen, email: cham@edu.au.dk, tel.: +45 6186 3645. 

The application must be submitted in English. 

About the Danish School of Education  

The Danish School of Education (DPU) is one of the three schools at the Faculty of Arts, Aarhus University. 

Across its two locations at Campus Emdrup in Copenhagen and Nobel Park in Aarhus, DPU is home to approximately 200 academic and administrative staff, as well as approximately 80 PhD students. 

Our degree programmes  

The Danish School of Education currently offers a Bachelor’s degree programme in educational studies and ten Master’s degree programmes in a range of educational and pedagogical disciplines, as well as six professional Master’s degree programmes that can also be studied as single-subject courses. 

Approximately 2,000 students are enrolled in the school’s Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes, with approximately 250 students enrolled in professional Master’s degree programmes. 

Many of these programmes are offered at DPU’s locations in both Copenhagen and Aarhus, with students fairly evenly divided between the two campuses. 

Our research  

The Danish School of Education is Denmark's largest university environment for basic and applied research in pedagogy and education. 

The school is home to strong research environments within educational studies, educational theory and curriculum studies, general education, educational psychology, educational anthropology, educational sociology and educational philosophy, 

In addition, we conduct interdisciplinary research focused on specific educational fields of inquiry, particularly schools and early childhood education and care. 

DPU promotes public awareness of research in education and pedagogy through extensive dissemination activities with the aim of providing society with a rich and robust knowledge base. 

International applicants  

International applicants are encouraged to read about family and work-life balance as well as the attractive working conditions and other benefits of working at Aarhus University and in Denmark, including healthcare, paid holidays and, if relevant, maternity/paternity leave, childcare and schooling. Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including a relocation service and career counselling for expat partners. For information about taxation, see the taxation aspects of international researchers’ employment by AU. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here: http://international.au.dk/research/ 

An appointee who does not speak Danish will be required to acquire proficiency in Danish to handle tasks, including administrative and managerial responsibilities, and to participate fully in the activities of the Danish School of Education within approximately two years of commencing the appointment. These activities include, but are not limited to, teaching and examining students, reading work-related texts and participating in meetings and collegial gatherings in Danish. 

Formalities
• Faculty of Arts refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities (the Appointment Order).
• Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.
• Further information on the application and supplementary materials may be found in Application Guidelines.
• The application must outline the applicant's motivation for applying for the position, attaching a curriculum vitae, a teaching portfolio, a complete list of published works, a research plan, copies of degree certificates and no more than five examples of academic production (mandatory).
Please upload this material electronically along with your application.

If nothing else is noted, applications must be submitted in English. Application deadline is at 11.59 pm Danish time (same as Central European Time) on the deadline day.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Shortlists may be prepared with the candidates that have been selected for a detailed academic assessment. A committee set up by the head of school is responsible for selecting the most qualified candidates. See this link for further information about shortlisting at the Faculty of Arts: shortlisting

Terms of employment
• Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations.
• Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as (xxx) at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).
The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

About ArtsThe Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. Within this broad academic scope, the faculty comprises approximately 700 researchers, 200 PhD students, 9,000 Bachelor’s and Master’s degree students, and 1,500 further and continuing education students. We believe that the best ideas arise when different perspectives meet – and that research, teaching and innovation are best developed in dialogue with the surrounding society.

You can find more information here: Faculty of Arts | Aarhus University

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Antifungal Resistance at the Food–Environment Interface - DTU Food
jobs.description:
Antimicrobial resistance is not just a bacterial problem. Antifungal resistance is an emerging threat to human health, yet we still know remarkably little about the occurrence and spread of resistant fungi across food production and associated environments, or what these reservoirs mean for human exposure and public health. Do you enjoy the lab bench as much as the command line, and would you like to help develop a new One Health surveillance framework? Then join us at DTU National Food Institute.

In this PhD project, you will investigate antifungal resistance at the food–environment interface, combining fungal isolation and susceptibility testing with genomics, bioinformatics and quantitative risk assessment. You will explore how resistant fungi occur and spread in food-production environments, investigate the genomic basis of antifungal resistance, and help translate surveillance data into estimates of human exposure and public-health impact. You will have real influence on the scientific direction of the project and help turn new knowledge into evidence that can support public-health and food-safety advice.

You will be supervised by an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in antimicrobial resistance, microbial genomics, bioinformatics and machine learning, quantitative risk assessment and burden-of-disease modelling.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall focus will be to generate new knowledge on antifungal resistance at the food–environment interface and assess its relevance for public health. You will be based in the Research Group for Global Capacity Building, collaborate closely with the Research Group for Risk-Benefit, and work in both the wet and the dry lab throughout the project. Your primary tasks will be to:

• Collect samples and isolate and characterise fungi from food and food-production environments, including antifungal susceptibility testing
• Generate and analyse whole-genome sequencing data to investigate antifungal resistance and genomic epidemiology in priority fungal pathogens, particularly Aspergillus fumigatus and Candida spp.
• Analyse complex microbial datasets, including metagenomic data where relevant
• Apply statistical and machine-learning approaches to investigate genotype–phenotype relationships and predict antifungal resistance from genomic data
• Contribute to probabilistic exposure and risk-assessment models linking surveillance data to public-health impact
• Communicate your research through publications and conferences, contribute to scientific advice, teaching, and co-supervision of BSc and MSc students
We are looking for a curious and motivated candidate who is interested in working across experimental microbiology and computational analysis. You do not need to be an expert in all aspects of the project when you start, but you should be enthusiastic about developing skills across both the wet and dry lab. You have:

• A master's degree in microbiology, molecular biology, biotechnology, bioinformatics, computational biology, or a related field
• Experience with bioinformatics and sequence analysis, including the analysis and interpretation of biological sequence data
• Experience with command-line computing, for example in a Linux environment
• Experience with scripting or statistical programming in a language such as Python or R
• Some hands-on experience with microbiological laboratory work, for example microbial cultivation, isolation, or phenotypic characterisation, together with an interest in further developing these skills
• An understanding of experimental design and basic statistical data analysis
• Good written and spoken English and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively
Experience with one or more of the following would be an advantage, but is not required: fungal microbiology, antimicrobial or antifungal susceptibility testing, whole-genome sequencing, metagenomics, microbial genomics, machine learning, or quantitative risk assessment.

In your cover letter, please describe your experience with laboratory and computational work and what interests you about combining these approaches in this project.

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Joana Mourão, Sara Monteiro Pires and René S. Hendriksen.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years.

Starting date is 1 January 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from the main supervisor, Joana Mourão (joam@food.dtu.dk), or the co-supervisors, Senior Researcher Sara Monteiro Pires (smpi@food.dtu.dk) and Professor René S. Hendriksen (rshe@food.dtu.dk). 

Read more about the Research Group for Global Capacity Building and the Research Group for Risk Benefit at https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/organisations/research-group-for-global-capacity-building/ and https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/organisations/research-group-for-risk-benefit/, respectively.

You can read more about DTU National Food Institute at www.food.dtu.dk/english 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 21 October 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• List of publications (if applicable)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU National Food Institute
DTU National Food Institute conducts research into and disseminates - through advice, innovation and teaching - sustainable and value-creating solutions in the area of food and health for the benefit of society. The vision is to make a difference by generating future prosperity through research into food and health. The institute works to prevent disease and promote health, develop new and better food products for a growing population and create sustainable technological solutions, including biosolutions. The institute’s tasks are carried out in interdisciplinary collaboration within e.g. nutrition, chemistry, toxicology, microbiology, epidemiology, modelling, and technology. This is achieved through a strong academic environment of international top class with correspondingly skilled researchers and employees. The Institute employs approximately 390 staff members.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

The Impact You'll Make

We are looking for a Mechanical Engineer to join Biomason’s production facility in Ikast.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is motivated by solving real technical challenges, improving operational and equipment reliability, and helping scale a first-of-a-kind process toward commercial production.

Do you have solid experience from an industrial or manufacturing environment, and do you thrive in a setting where not everything has been fully built or established yet? Then we would very much like to hear from you.

👉 Read more about the role in the below job description.

If you have technical questions, you are welcome to contact Director of Plant Performance Aaron Bellis at +45 28966291 or HR Partner René Bitsch at +45 21756113.

If you are from a recruitment agency please note that we will contact you if we need your assistance.

Job description

The position:

As Mechanical engineer, you will play a hands-on role in establishing, stabilizing, and improving the mechanical performance of our first-of-a-kind tile production facility in Ikast. This role will work closely together with Operations, Maintenance, Quality, and Process Engineering to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient plant performance. You will help translate innovative process science into robust day-to-day manufacturing at the first of a kind facility, while driving structured problem-solving, equipment reliability, ppm, plant expansion support, and continuous improvement across the facility.

You will support the scaling of this process to our first commercial facility from engineering design and equipment selection through commissioning, start-up, and operations working together with our project department and our EPC firms.

Responsibilities also include:

• 
Mechanical Operations & Equipment Reliability

• 
Provide day-to-day supervisory and execution support for electrical and mechanical systems and production equipment across the tile manufacturing process.

• 
Lead troubleshooting and root cause analysis for mechanical failures, downtime events, and recurring equipment issues.

• 
Help establish preventive and predictive maintenance routines for critical equipment, utilities, and production assets.

• 
Support commissioning, start-up, and scale-up activities in a FOAK environment, helping to translate development work into reliable plant operation.

• 
Production Support & Continuous Improvement

• 
Partner with Operations and Quality teams to improve equipment performance, uptime, process stability, and product consistency.

• 
Contribute to waste reduction, line efficiency, and standardization efforts as production scales.

• 
  Technical leadership

• 
Support the development of SOPs, technical work instructions, equipment care standards, and troubleshooting guides.

• 
Coordinate with vendors, contractors, and internal teams on equipment modifications, installation work, and performance improvements.

• 
Project engineering and commercial facility scale-up

• 
With the Director of projects and an EPC firm, act as Biomason’s lead mechanical engineer supporting the development of FEL3 and detailed engineering design packages including participation in and review of Block Flow Diagrams (BFDs), Heat and Material Balances (HMBs), Piping and Instrumentation Diagrams (P&IDs), General Arrangements (GAs), Basis of Design (BoD) documents, equipment specification and selection, and HAZOP (Hazard an Operations study).

• 
Support the commissioning and startup of the commercial facility through:

• 
Participation in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) at vendor sites as needed and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) at the facility.

• 
Provide on-site technical leadership during the "boots-on-the-ground" commissioning phase, troubleshooting mechanical, thermal, or other deviations in real-time.

• 
Bridge the gap between EPC firms and internal operations to ensure a seamless handover.

What we are looking for:

• 
Experience

• 
Minimum 5 years of experience in mechanical engineering, maintenance engineering, or a similar industrial role.

• 
Strong experience in industrial process or manufacturing environments, ideally with automated or semi-automated production equipment. Concrete manufacturing or other heavy industry is bonus but not essential.

• 
Experience with motors, heat exchangers, airflow and hydraulics is a strong advantage.

• 
Basic electrical experience testing logout tag out.

• 
Experience supporting production start-ups, greenfield projects, FOAK environments, or first-time industrial implementation is strongly preferred.

• 
Technical Expertise

• 
Experience working with crane and conveyance systems is a critical requirement of this position

• 
Strong understanding of industrial mechanical systems, equipment reliability, maintenance strategies, and structured troubleshooting.

• 
Experience with 5S, good manufacturing practices, and continuous improvement in a production setting.

• 
Ability to read technical drawings, manuals, equipment layouts, P&IDs, and supplier documentation.

• 
Familiarity with Six Sigma, Lean manufacturing principles, root cause analysis methodologies, and continuous improvement practices is an advantage.

• 
Management & Interpersonal Skills

• 
High attention to detail, with the ability to manage complex, detail-oriented projects and ensure disciplined follow-up through execution.

• 
Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work across functions and cultures, preferable experience from a matrix organization..

• 
Structured, practical, and data-informed approach to problem-solving and decision-making.

• 
Contractor control

• 
Fluency in English is essential

On a personal level, the role needs the following approach:

• 
Proactive with a practical approach and the ability to be hands-on 

• 
Motivation to solve real industrial challenges

• 
Flexible where systems and routines are still being built

• 
A collaborative mindset, but also the ability to solve matters on your own

• 
Good safety attitude

• 
Can do attitude

jobs.description:
At Bavarian Nordic, we are committed to saving and improving lives by unlocking the power of the immune system. Our commercial portfolio includes market-leading vaccines against smallpox/mpox, rabies, tick-borne encephalitis, typhoid fever, and cholera. We excel in R&D innovation, manufacturing, and commercialization, working every day to protect people’s health and quality of life and protect our tomorrow.

We are looking for an experienced leader for the Head of Center of Excellence (project management) role in our Strategy Execution department who combines strategic thinking, strong change management capabilities, and a genuine passion for building organizational capability. In this role, you will not only define how projects are governed and delivered but also drive the adoption of new ways of working across a global organization.

**About The Role

**This is a broad and hands-on role spanning project leadership and organizational capability building within project excellence. A key aspect of the role is driving organizational change by ensuring that project management frameworks, tools, and processes are successfully adopted, understood, and embedded across the business. In this dual role, you will balance being Head of Center of Excellence while managing high-impact cross-functional projects yourself. Just as importantly, you will turn standards into practice by designing and delivering training, facilitating sessions, coaching colleagues, and creating engagement across the organization.

You will work across R&D, manufacturing, supply chain, commercial, and corporate functions. The portfolio may include merger and acquisition activities, development projects, vaccine launches, technology implementations, and other enterprise-wide transformation initiatives. Success requires someone who enjoys moving between strategic planning, practical implementation, and visible facilitation in front of an audience.

The position is based in Hellerup, Denmark. You will join a team of +20 Project Managers, Program Leads, and Student Assistants and report to the VP of Strategy Execution Office.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own and continuously strengthen project management standards, governance, tools, templates, and ways of working across the organization

• Lead complex, cross-functional strategic projects, including initiatives connected to M&A, product development, vaccine launches, and enterprise transformation

• Drive adoption of project management methodologies and support organizational change through stakeholder engagement, communication, training, and coaching

• Develop project management capability through structured training, facilitation, coaching, and hands-on knowledge sharing across different functions and seniority levels

• Serve as a visible ambassador for project excellence, translating methodology into clear, practical, and engaging learning experiences

• Partner with senior stakeholders to create alignment, transparency, sound decision-making, and clear ownership throughout the project lifecycle

• Drive disciplined planning, risk management, resource coordination, and execution, supported by strong use of project and portfolio management tools

**What You Bring

**You bring extensive experience leading complex projects within pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, vaccines, or another highly regulated healthcare environment. You also bring change management expertise combined with hands-on delivery experience. Besides this, we are looking for someone with the following background;

• A genuine interest in the full scope of project management excellence, from strategic framework design and governance to practical implementation and organizational training

• Strong presentation and facilitation skills, with the confidence and energy to stand in front of an audience, engage participants, and make complex methods practical and relevant

• Demonstrated ability to influence senior stakeholders, create buy-in, and lead through complex global and cross-functional environments

• Strong knowledge of PMI-based project management practices. PMI/PMP certification is an advantage - other relevant certifications are also valued

• Experience with merger and acquisition projects

• A relevant master’s degree within life sciences, engineering, supply chain, business, or a related field

• Advanced expertise in Smartsheet combined with experience with Microsoft Project is an advantage

**Why join us?

**This role gives you the opportunity to influence both how strategic projects are delivered and how project management capability is built across Bavarian Nordic. You will combine high-impact project leadership with the chance to shape standards, develop colleagues, and create a lasting project excellence culture in a purpose-driven global vaccine organization.

If you are motivated by strategy and execution, enjoy building practical solutions, and feel energized by training and engaging others, we would love to hear from you.

**Caught your interest?

**Apply now and join Bavarian Nordic in our mission to improve health outcomes and foster sustainable growth.

We do not offer any relocation packages for this role. Please note that employment is contingent on residing and working in Denmark.

We kindly request that headhunters or recruitment agencies refrain from contacting us regarding this position.

_Bavarian Nordic is a global vaccine company with a mission to improve health and save lives through innovative vaccines. We are a preferred supplier of mpox and smallpox vaccines to governments to enhance public health preparedness and have a leading portfolio of travel vaccines. We are headquartered in Denmark and have manufacturing, research, and sales offices across Europe and North America.

__Bavarian Nordic is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applications will receive consideration for employment and will not be discriminated against based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

_For more information, visit www.bavarian-nordic.com

Would you like to manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets – and use your quantitative skills to make better commercial decisions?

Join our Physical Asset Management team and take responsibility for your own areas of the portfolio. You will work hands-on with market analysis, quantitative models, pricing and PnL while building the market knowledge needed to spot where we can do things better.

The team

You will join Physical Asset Management at Norlys Energy Trading in Aalborg. We manage renewable energy portfolios across European power markets, combining portfolio management with market analysis and quantitative methods. The work involves close interaction with colleagues across trading, origination and asset management.

The role

As a Quant Researcher, you will operate and develop parts of our renewable portfolio across Europe. Over time, you will become the go-to person for your areas of responsibility: understanding what moves the market, how it affects the portfolio and where there is room to improve performance.

The role has a strong quantitative element. You will build models to understand portfolio effects, develop PnL dashboards and work on pricing methodologies and trading automation. You will also investigate new markets and products and help turn promising ideas into new business.

Key responsibilities

The role combines running the portfolio today with improving how we work tomorrow. You will work independently on some areas and together with colleagues and stakeholders in others.

• Maintain and operate our renewable portfolios across the EU.

• Run your own areas of responsibility with a focus on profitable performance.

• Follow your markets closely and build specialist knowledge within your areas.

• Build and maintain quantitative models to analyse and optimise portfolio effects.

• Develop pricing methodologies and identify ways to improve portfolio performance.

• Build and maintain dashboards that show PnL for your portfolios.

• Help automate trading tools and processes.

• Investigate new markets and products that could create new business opportunities. Work closely with key stakeholders and take part in relevant conferences and excursions.

The people who thrive in this kind of role are the ones who stay curious when the answer isn’t obvious. You’ll have room to dig into problems, form your own view and act on what you learn. And when the market changes, you need to be comfortable changing your mind with it.

Peter Lumbye Thomsen

Head of Intraday Analytics

What we are looking for

You are comfortable working with numbers, code and complex market information, but analysis is not an end in itself for you. You want to use it to make decisions, improve the way we work and move things forward when the market changes.

We expect you to have:

• An advanced degree in a quantitative field such as physics, economics, data science or mathematics.

• Strong programming skills in Python, R or a similar language.

• Experience with data analysis and statistical modelling.

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

• A can-do attitude and a sense of urgency when something needs to move.

• An understanding of why agility and speed-to-market matter in a changing market.

• The ability to work well with different stakeholders in a fast-paced environment.

• Experience within power trading or finance is an advantage, but not a requirement.

What we offer

• The role gives you room to build specialist knowledge while working hands-on with renewable portfolios across European power markets.

• Your own areas of responsibility within renewable portfolio management.

• The chance to build specialist knowledge of European power markets.

• A role that combines quantitative work with commercial decision-making.

• Exposure to new markets, products and business opportunities.

• Close collaboration with colleagues and stakeholders across the business.

• Participation in relevant conferences and excursions.

Interested?

If the combination of power markets, quantitative analysis and portfolio responsibility sounds like a good match for you, we would like to hear from you.

Want to know more?

Feel free to reach out if you have any questions about this opportunity

Peter Lumbye Thomsen

Head of Intraday Analytics

About the Job:

Join our team as a passionate and experienced Cyber Security Analyst to help safeguard our digital assets. In this role, you will focus on alert triage, incident response, and enhancing our Security Operations Centre (SOC).

Our multinational team leverages a diverse array of security tools, offering you a dynamic environment for learning and growth. We collaborate to investigate in-depth, with a goal to keep Saxo safe from external threats targeting our environments. You will become part of our ongoing efforts to enhance our forensic capabilities and leverage SOAR to automate triage workflows and improve detections.

Key Responsibilities:

In this role, you will be responsible for monitoring and triaging security alerts to keep our defences sharp. Additionally, you will get the opportunity to lead and conduct forensic investigations to uncover, understand and mitigate threats. Collaboration is key, as you will work closely with team members, our threat intelligence and Insider Threat team, Saxo organizational stakeholders, and external security partners to strengthen our security posture.

Further;

• Build and maintain operational awareness through trend analysis, dashboards, and reports for the C-suite.

• Mentor team members and conduct knowledge-sharing sessions to foster a culture of continuous improvement.

• Provide input to automation, enhancing detections, playbooks, and our security technology stack.

• Monitor, perform, and improve security controls to ensure robust protection.

• Investigative and triage assistance to our Insider Threat team

Your Profile:

You should have over 5 years of experience in the cybersecurity domain, demonstrating a proactive and diligent work ethic with an eye for detail. Your approach to tasks is marked by curiosity, creativity, and structure. Proficiency in one or more areas of cybersecurity forensics, such as binary triage, network log analysis, host forensics, and/or threat intelligence, is essential.

Experience with SIEM/SOAR platforms, endpoint security platforms, AI-enabled investigations, and ServiceNow or other ticketing platforms is required. Additionally, familiarity with SOAR playbooks, automation, and alert fine-tuning is a plus. Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, or SANS are advantageous.

Last day for applying is 21st of October 2026.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

Would you like to take the lead in turning business opportunities into digital solutions that create measurable commercial impact?

As Digital Business Transformation Lead, you will help execute Hartmann’s European commercial strategy by identifying, shaping and delivering digital initiatives that improve customer experience and commercial efficiency. Reporting to the Commercial Excellence Director, Europe, you will work across markets and functions to turn business needs into practical solutions with measurable impact.

You will own the business side of agreed initiatives from discovery and concept development through implementation, adoption and benefits realisation. Group IT and technology partners will own architecture, cybersecurity and technical solution design.

Key responsibilities

• Identify and evaluate digital opportunities with customers and stakeholders across Hartmann’s European commercial organisation.

• Translate needs into customer journeys, future-state processes, concepts, prototypes and business requirements.

• Build business cases and support prioritisation of the European commercial digital portfolio.

• Lead the business side of agreed initiatives from discovery through implementation and adoption.

• Establish milestones, governance, risks, responsibilities and benefits tracking.

• Partner with Group IT and external providers while keeping customer needs and business outcomes central.

• Drive adoption through stakeholder engagement, communication, training and performance measurement.

Your experience and approach

We expect you to have:

• Experience taking unclear opportunities from discovery to implementation and adoption

jobs.occupation: Take ownership of AML, KYC, risk and compliance in Secure Payment (part of AutoProff)
jobs.description:
Secure Payment is the payment entity within AutoProff, handling payments related to our car auctions across the business. We’re looking for a AML, KYC, Risk & Compliance Specialist to take ownership of our compliance framework and help ensure that Secure Payment remains well governed, structured and compliant as we continue to develop the business.

This is a broad and hands-on role where you’ll work closely with management, the Board of Directors and colleagues across Tech, Support and Finance.

At AutoProff, we’re changing the way used vehicles are traded across Europe. Every day, thousands of vehicles are bought and sold through our platform, connecting professional car dealers across markets.

About the role

As our new AML, KYC, Risk & Compliance Specialist, you’ll join Secure Payment and be based at our headquarters in Vejle, Denmark.

You’ll take responsibility for AML, KYC, risk and compliance activities and help ensure that policies, processes, controls and documentation are kept up to date and work effectively in practice.

The role has a broad stakeholder landscape and combines structured compliance work with reporting, administration and practical follow-up. You’ll work closely with the Board of Directors, management, customers and colleagues across AutoProff, including Tech, Support and Finance.

Secure Payment is also developing a new reporting methodology, and you’ll have the opportunity to help shape how we structure management information, controls and reporting going forward.

What you’ll be doing

Your responsibilities will include:

• Own and further develop Secure Payment’s AML, KYC, risk and compliance activities

• Maintain and improve relevant policies, procedures, controls and documentation

• Coordinate and follow up on KYC reviews, customer due diligence, monitoring and relevant AML cases

• Identify, assess and follow up on compliance and operational risks

• Prepare clear and structured reporting for management and the Board of Directors

• Help develop Secure Payment’s reporting methodology and management information

• Follow up on findings, incidents, regulatory requirements and agreed actions

• Work closely with colleagues across Tech, Support, Finance and the wider AutoProff organisation

• Explore how AI and digital tools can support reporting, documentation and compliance processes

• Maintain constructive dialogue with relevant internal and external stakeholders

What we’re looking for

We imagine you have experience with AML and KYC, or a solid understanding of the underlying principles combined with a strong interest in developing your regulatory and legal knowledge further.

More specifically, we’re looking for someone with:

• Experience with AML, KYC or related compliance activities

• A structured and administrative approach to work

• Strong attention to detail and a focus on high-quality documentation and reporting

• The ability to maintain an overview and prioritise when several tasks are moving at the same time

• An interest in compliance, risk and regulatory topics

• Good understanding of IT systems and digital tools

• Strong written and verbal communication skills in Danish and English

• Confidence working independently and taking ownership of your area

Beyond your experience, we’re looking for someone who is structured, curious and hands-on, and who enjoys creating order, following up and making sure things are done properly.

Nice to have

It’s a plus, but not a requirement, if you have experience with:

• Banking, payment institutions, financial services or another regulated environment

• Risk and compliance in a regulated business

• Reporting to senior management or a Board of Directors

• A banking or financial-services background

• Using AI or digital tools to improve reporting, documentation or compliance processes

Why join AutoProff?

At AutoProff, you’ll become part of an international company that is changing the way used cars are traded across Europe.

You’ll work with colleagues across countries and functions in an environment where there is room to take ownership, share ideas and influence how we do things. We move quickly, work closely together and value people who are comfortable taking responsibility while also asking for input when needed.

As part of AutoScout24 Group, we combine the pace and hands-on environment of AutoProff with the opportunities and international reach of one of Europe’s leading automotive marketplaces.

In this role, you’ll have the opportunity to shape a developing compliance function, work closely with senior stakeholders and influence how Secure Payment structures its AML, KYC, risk and reporting processes going forward.

Ready to join us?

If this sounds like an opportunity you’d like to explore, we’d like to hear from you.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the position once we have found the right candidate.

About AutoProff

AutoProff was founded in Denmark in 2013 with one goal: to make B2B used-car trading simpler and more efficient through digital solutions.

Today, AutoProff provides online B2B used-car trading solutions for professional car dealers across Europe, with more than 150,000 vehicles traded through our platforms annually.

In August 2022, AutoScout24, one of Europe’s leading online automotive marketplaces, acquired a majority stake in AutoProff. Together, we are working towards creating a fully integrated C2B-B2B-B2C solution for used cars across Europe.

Our ambition is simple: to be the home of B2B car trading for European car dealers.

Shape the future of trusted digital signing

Join Cryptomathic's Signer team and help build secure software that enables trusted digital signatures and seals for governments, financial institutions, and trust service providers worldwide.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you'll work on a complex, business-critical platform where security, reliability, and compliance are essential. You'll be part of a small, experienced team with significant influence over technical decisions while remaining hands-on and close to the code.

About Signer

Signer is Cryptomathic's electronic signing platform, enabling trust service providers, governments, and financial institutions to deliver legally binding electronic signatures and seals. Built on industry standards and aligned with eIDAS, Signer helps customers implement trusted digital signing solutions at scale while meeting demanding security and compliance requirements.

What you'll do

As a member of the Signer team, you will work on a product at the intersection of security, cryptography, cloud technologies, and enterprise integrations. You will help evolve a platform used in highly regulated industries where reliability, security, and performance are non-negotiable.

As a senior member of the team, you will help shape our technical direction and contribute to feature design, backlog refinement, estimation, and the continuous improvement of our development practices.

Who you are

Most importantly, you are an experienced developer who enjoys staying close to the code. You enjoy solving difficult technical problems and understand that great software is built by strong teams.

You take ownership, stay with challenges until they are properly resolved, and remain constructive when things get complicated.

You share knowledge, support colleagues, and are comfortable challenging existing approaches when you see a better way forward. And you are a team player who cares about the overall result, not only your own tasks, and contributes to an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Ideally, you have:

• At least five years of professional experience developing software

• Strong hands-on Java development experience

• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be an advantage:

• Cryptography, PKI, digital signatures, or other security-sensitive software solutions

• Experience using AI-assisted development tools pragmatically to improve efficiency while maintaining high standards of software quality and security

You do not need to tick every box. If you are a strong Java developer with an interest in secure software and a willingness to learn, we would still like to hear from you.

Why you might enjoy working with us

You will join a small, experienced team where your contribution is visible, and your technical judgement matters. You will have the opportunity to stay close to the code while influencing how we design features, improve the codebase, and evolve our development practices.

Signer offers technically demanding work at the intersection of Java, security, cryptography, and digital trust. You will work alongside experienced colleagues and have the opportunity to deepen your expertise in a highly specialized domain.

Our Aarhus development office has a collaborative and informal working environment built on openness, knowledge sharing, and pragmatic problem-solving. We care about building reliable software, supporting one another, and continuously improving how we work.

Product Portfolio Support Manager, Wound and Tissue Repair Product Management team

Are you ready to join the Wound and Tissue Repair team making an impact for people living with wounds?

Make a difference together with us

You will join an international Product Management team of highly dedicated colleagues. Based in Humlebæk, the team is part of the Product Strategy and Development team. Together, we set the strategic direction, drive global product launches and maximise the potential of the existing WTR portfolio.

We collaborate with colleagues around the world and across organizational levels and functions, including R&D, Global Operations, Marketing and Sales.

In this role, you will work closely with Product Managers to ensure efficient portfolio operations across the WTR portfolio. Alongside supporting shared priorities, you will independently lead defined projects and workstreams from planning through execution and follow-up.

Your role – enabling portfolio excellence and driving projects

Your responsibilities will include:

•    Act as a key point of contact for markets and cross-functional stakeholders, independently resolving routine portfolio questions and coordinating input when broader alignment is needed

•    Lead defined portfolio projects and smaller workstreams independently, including scoping, planning, stakeholder alignment, execution, risk management and follow-up

•    Support processes and system tasks

•    Support MDR activities and claiming document reviews

•    Own and coordinate IFU and labelling updates, ensuring alignment across relevant stakeholders and systems.

•    Support quality reviews and supply chain processes

•    Support internal and external events

•    Drive planning and follow-ups from team meetings

Who you are

•    Experience coordinating portfolio activities and independently leading projects or workstreams from initial scope through delivery and follow-up

•    Strong stakeholder management and communication skills

•    Structured, proactive, and detail-oriented

•    A passion for collaboration

•    Comfortable working with complexity in a dynamic environment

•    Fluent in English

•    Experience from healthcare or medtech is an advantage

What we offer

•    A central role in a growing and high-impact area

•    Close collaboration with experienced colleagues

•    Broad exposure to portfolio management

•    Opportunities for growth

Interested?

If this sounds like a fit, we would love to hear from you. If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Nayla Ayoub, Head of Product Management- Wound and Tissue Repair, at dknaay@coloplast.com .

We will take candidates into the recruitment process continuously, so do not hesitate to apply. This position will remain open until a suitable candidate is found.

Pursuing an ambitious growth agenda, Coloplast develops and markets products and services that make life easier for people with intimate healthcare needs. Employing about 16.000 people and with products available in more than 143 countries, we are one of the world´s leading medical device companies. We are constantly growing our business and always looking for new ways to move forward – we explore, learn and look for new ways of doing things.

Coloplast is committed to being an inclusive organization, where people bring their differences to work each day, fulfil their potential and have a strong sense of belonging because – and not despite – of their differences. We therefore encourage all qualified candidates to apply regardless of gender, age, race, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religious belief or physical ability.

jobs.occupation: Social Media & Influencer Specialist for PlayStation, Nordisk Interactive
jobs.description:
Role title: Brand Engagement & Community Specialist

Contract: Fixed-term maternity cover

Contract period: 1st of January 2027 – 1st of February 2028

Location: Nordisk Interactive, Valby, Copenhagen

Working model: Hybrid

Do you love gaming, social media and creator culture - and do you know how to make a global brand feel local?

We are looking for a Brand Engagement & Community Specialist for Denmark to join PlayStation Nordic as a fixed-term maternity cover from 1st January 2027 to 1st of February 2028.

This role sits in our Marketing team and is all about bringing PlayStation closer to players every day through social media, influencer collaborations, local content and community management.

This is a hands-on role. You will not just sit in meetings talking about campaigns. You will help make them happen.

You will work closely with our Leads across social media, PR, influencers, brand partnerships, sponsorships and campaigns - and you will be one of the people making sure PlayStation shows up in a way that feels relevant, local and real.

**What you'll be doing

**Social media, content and community

You will help run PlayStation’s Danish social channels day to day. That means planning, publishing, adapting content, engaging with the community and making sure our tone feels right for our Danish audience.

You will work with global assets, Danish ideas and real-time opportunities across channels like Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and other relevant platforms.

In practice, this means:

• Adapting global PlayStation content so it works in Danish language, tone and context

• Supporting the local social media calendar

• Publishing and scheduling content (in collaboration with student assistant)

• Managing community engagement and comments

• Spotting local trends and moments we can react to

• Supporting live coverage around events, campaigns and sponsorships

• Making sure our content feels like PlayStation, but also like it belongs locally

You will also collaborate with the Danish student assistant on relevant tasks such as translations, content adaptations and community work.

Influencers and creators

Creators are a big part of how we bring PlayStation to life in the Nordics. You will support our local influencer work, from finding the right profiles to briefing, seeding and following up on content.

You will work closely with our PR & Influencer Lead, but you will also be expected to take ownership of the day-to-day coordination in the Danish market.

This includes:

• Building and maintaining relationships with Danish creators and PlayStation Playmakers

• Supporting influencer briefings, seedings and content follow-up

• Coordinating products, merchandise and hardware where relevant

• Tracking creator content and helping report on performance

• Making sure creators are properly briefed and aligned with PlayStation guidelines

Campaign and partnership support

You will be involved in some of the biggest PlayStation moments of the year. That can be major game launches, hardware pushes, UEFA sponsorship activations, retail collaborations, influencer events or local content ideas.

You will help turn strategy into actual execution.

That means:

• Supporting priority campaigns in the Danish market

• Contributing with local ideas and cultural input

• Helping execute brand partnership and sponsorship activations

• Supporting events, press moments and consumer activations

• Working in Monday.com to keep tasks, owners and deadlines clear

• Making sure local execution is on time and on brief

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who is structured, curious and genuinely interested in gaming, social media and online communities.

You do not need to know everything from day one. But you do need to be proactive, willing to learn and comfortable working in a team where many things move at the same time.

You probably bring:

• Danish at native level, especially written Danish

• Strong English skills

• Good understanding of social media and creator culture

• A strong feel for what works in Denmark

• Good writing skills and attention to tone of voice

• Confidence in coordinating tasks and keeping projects moving

• Good attention to detail

• Ability to work with several stakeholders at once

• Interest in gaming, entertainment and online communities

• Experience with social media, influencer work, content production, communications or marketing

• Familiarity with tools like Monday.com, Upfluence or Emplifi is a plus, but not a requirement

Most importantly, you are someone people enjoy working with. We need someone who can take responsibility, communicate clearly and help make the team better.

What can you expect?

You will join a team that cares deeply about PlayStation, but also about doing good work together.

We are a Nordic team working across multiple markets, cultures and disciplines. Some days are structured. Some days are messy. That is part of the job. But you will be close to great campaigns, major game launches, creators, communities and some of the biggest entertainment moments of the year.

You will get responsibility, trust and room to contribute.

Application task

Please apply by using the "Apply Now". We do not receive applications via. e-mail.

As part of your application, we would like you to include a short video of max. 1 minute.

In the video, please answer this question in Danish:

_• Tell us about something you are proud of creating, improving or making happen.

_

This does not need to be professionally produced. We are not looking for editing skills or a polished influencer video. We are interested in how you think and how you communicate.

Our application system cannot receive video files, so please upload the video to YouTube, Vimeo or a similar platform and include the link in your application. An unlisted link is completely fine.

Application deadline is 22/10/2026.

About Nordisk Film

Nordisk Film was founded in 1906 in Valby, by entrepreneur Ole Olsen and is one of the world’s first film companies. They still have their headquarters in Valby, next to the world’s oldest film studio building and still own strong cultural values of passion and ambition.

In 1992, Nordisk Film became part of Egmont, a Nordic media group, and has within recent years seen high growth rates. In just over five years their revenues have increased with nearly 40%, and activities now span much wider than the film business that was the starting point. Today, Nordisk Film is among the leading entertainment companies in the Nordics involved in film and series production and distribution, cinemas, computer games, digital gifting and digital advertising.

For more than 20 years, and since the launch of Sony PlayStation, Nordisk Film Interactive has been the official distributor of the console and games in the Nordics and Baltics, and have made it one of Sony’s most successful markets.

Join us in this role where you’ll trade green certificates from Ørsted’s renewable portfolio while helping identify and execute commercial opportunities across European markets. You’ll work closely with colleagues, customers, and counterparties to optimise revenue streams, expand trading activities, and support value creation through market insight and commercial execution.

Welcome to Trading & Revenue

You’ll be part of Green Certificates where you, together with your colleagues, will optimise revenue streams and create value from Ørsted’s portfolio of green certificates linked to renewable energy generation across Europe. The team manages trading activities, develops commercial opportunities, and builds strong market relationships to maximise value across our certificate portfolio. As a team, we collaborate closely, challenge each other constructively, and combine commercial curiosity with a shared ambition to deliver strong results.

You’ll play an important role in:

• trading ROCs, REGOs, GoOs, and other green certificates from Ørsted’s European renewable portfolio through active participation in the market

• identifying and executing trading opportunities that create value across certificate markets and customer segments

• building and strengthening relationships with existing and new trading counterparties across Europe

• analysing market developments, regulatory changes, and pricing dynamics to support trading decisions

• collaborating with colleagues across Trading & Revenue to optimise portfolio performance and commercial outcomes

• supporting the development and expansion of Green Certificates trading activities and products.

To succeed in the role, you:

• bring experience from certificate trading, power trading, commodity markets, treasury and trading, or equivalent commercial environments

• have a strong understanding of energy markets, market fundamentals, and value creation through trading activities

• can analyse market information and translate insights into commercially sound decisions

• build trusted relationships with customers, counterparties, and internal stakeholders across a complex organisation

• navigate negotiations, commercial agreements, and risk considerations with confidence and integrity

• hold a degree in finance, economics, business, engineering, or equivalent experience.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

Shape the future with us

Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country.

Build the team that builds Relesys. We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager to lead and develop one of our engineering teams.

You’ll be accountable for the team’s growth, performance and delivery, creating the conditions for engineers to do their best work and deliver meaningful customer and business outcomes sustainably. You’ll also help the team adopt AI effectively in software development and explore opportunities for AI-powered product innovation.

You turn strategy into a small set of clear priorities, make the trade-offs behind them visible, and create the planning and release rhythm that lets your area ship reliably. You stay accountable for architecture decisions, production health, security posture and technical debt - even when senior engineers are leading the actual design work - and you make sure delivery is backed by solid fundamentals: testing, observability, feature flags, and real incident learning.

This is an exciting and transformative time to join Relesys, as we have gone into a strategic partnership with the Private Equity fund, Copilot Capital, where the coming years will bring extensive growth and opportunities along the way. You get a unique opportunity to make a tremendous impact in taking your career, Relesys and our dear clients to the next level over the coming years - as we say, joining a scale-up at this stage is a rare opportunity that is “once in a lifetime”.

Your key responsibilities

• 
Lead and develop your people: Hold regular one-on-ones, provide timely and actionable feedback, and coach engineers through technical, professional and interpersonal challenges.

• 
Own career development and performance: Set clear expectations and individual development goals, conduct performance reviews, support progression and promotion decisions, and address underperformance early and constructively.

• 
Build a healthy, effective team: Foster trust, inclusion and accountability, resolve conflict, and actively support engagement, wellbeing and sustainable workloads.

• 
Hire and onboard engineers: Partner with People & Talent on hiring, plan team capabilities and capacity, and help new colleagues become effective contributors.

• 
Turn strategy into a small set of clear, prioritized outcomes for your area, and make the trade-offs behind them visible

• 
Create planning and release rhythms that make delivery more predictable, without relying on heavy process or overtime

• 
Own architecture trade-offs, production health, security posture and technical-debt decisions for your area - even when senior engineers lead the actual design

• 
Make sure delivery is backed by solid engineering fundamentals: testing, observability, feature flags, and real incident learning

• 
Use delivery, operational and customer evidence to continuously adjust plans and priorities

• 
Drive AI-assisted engineering: Help the team evaluate and adopt AI tools across development, testing, code review and documentation. Build practical skills, establish appropriate quality and data-handling practices, and assess their impact on delivery and maintainability.

• 
Enable AI product innovation: Partner with Product, Design and engineers to identify valuable AI use cases, run focused experiments, and take promising solutions into production with clear evaluation criteria for customer value, reliability, privacy and cost.

Relesys isn't just another SaaS company; we are a dynamic force revolutionizing communication and performance management platforms. Established in 2014, we set out on a mission to bridge the gap between HQ and non-desk workers, fostering a thriving workforce.
